title: CHW Diabetes Self-Management Support
recommendation_text: Conduct monthly home visits to provide culturally tailored diabetes education, medication adherence support, and blood glucose monitoring guidance. Connect patients to community resources for nutrition and physical activity programs.
implementation_guidance: Schedule 60-90 minute monthly visits using validated DSMES curriculum. Provide blood glucose meter training and supplies. Create personalized action plans with patients. Maintain updated directory of local food assistance and exercise programs.
expected_outcomes: 0.5-1.0% reduction in HbA1c levels (95% CI: 0.3-1.2%), improved medication adherence >80%, increased self-monitoring frequency, 22% reduction in diabetes-related hospitalizations. Number needed to treat (NNT): 8 patients to prevent one hospitalization.
citation_authors: Community Preventive Services Task Force
citation_title: Diabetes Management: Interventions Engaging Community Health Workers
target_population: Medicaid, underserved communities
cost_effectiveness: Cost-effective at $585/person/year

title: Doula Prenatal Support
recommendation_text: Provide minimum 4 prenatal visits offering childbirth education, emotional support, birth plan development, and healthcare system navigation. Focus on culturally competent care and patient advocacy throughout pregnancy.
implementation_guidance: Schedule initial visit by 28 weeks gestation. Conduct 2-3 additional prenatal visits (60-90 minutes each). Develop personalized birth plan with patient preferences. Coordinate with prenatal care providers. Provide 24/7 on-call availability starting at 37 weeks.
expected_outcomes: 53% reduction in cesarean delivery rates (95% CI: 42-64%), 57% reduction in postpartum depression/anxiety diagnosis, increased breastfeeding initiation rates, higher maternal satisfaction scores. NNT: 6 patients to prevent one cesarean delivery.
citation_authors: Falconi AM, Bromfield N, Felder JN, Elder J, Giurgescu C
citation_title: The effect of doula care on birth outcomes in Medicaid populations: A systematic review
target_population: Medicaid-enrolled pregnant individuals
cost_effectiveness: Cost savings of $986 per birth

title: Nurse Hypertension Management
recommendation_text: Lead multidisciplinary hypertension management team using standardized medication titration protocols, lifestyle counseling, and regular follow-up monitoring. Coordinate care with pharmacists, CHWs, and dietitians.
implementation_guidance: Implement evidence-based protocols for BP management using collaborative practice agreements. Schedule structured follow-up visits every 2-4 weeks until BP goal achieved. Use electronic health records for population health monitoring and outreach.
expected_outcomes: 70-80% of patients achieve BP goal (<130/80 mmHg) compared to 30-40% with usual care (95% CI: 35-45% improvement), reduced clinical inertia in medication management, improved provider efficiency. NNT: 3 patients to achieve one additional BP control.
citation_authors: Community Preventive Services Task Force
citation_title: Cardiovascular Disease: Team-Based Care to Improve Blood Pressure Control
target_population: Adults with uncontrolled hypertension
cost_effectiveness: Cost savings of $2,500-$4,000 per patient annually

title: Pharmacist Medication Therapy Management
recommendation_text: Conduct quarterly comprehensive medication reviews for patients with diabetes taking multiple medications, focusing on adherence barriers, drug interactions, and therapy optimization. Provide medication action plans and communicate recommendations to primary care providers.
implementation_guidance: Schedule 45-60 minute initial consultations followed by 20-30 minute quarterly follow-ups. Use standardized documentation templates for medication reviews. Implement collaborative practice agreements for medication adjustments. Provide direct patient education on proper medication use.
expected_outcomes: 0.8% mean reduction in HbA1c (95% CI: 0.5-1.1%), 35% improvement in medication adherence rates, 42% reduction in medication-related problems. NNT: 12 patients to prevent one diabetes-related emergency department visit.
citation_authors: Jeong S, Patel I, Hata M, Arnall J, Hwang W, Jones C, Choi Y
citation_title: Clinical and economic outcomes of pharmacist-led medication therapy management for patients with type 2 diabetes: A systematic review and meta-analysis
citation_journal: Research in Social and Administrative Pharmacy
target_population: Adults with type 2 diabetes on multiple medications
cost_effectiveness: Return on investment of $3.30 for every $1 spent

title: CHW Blood Pressure Self-Monitoring
recommendation_text: Implement home blood pressure monitoring program with bi-weekly CHW support visits to validate technique, review readings, and provide lifestyle modification coaching. Establish clear protocols for when patients should contact healthcare providers based on BP thresholds.
implementation_guidance: Provide validated home BP monitors and train patients on proper measurement technique. Create standardized BP log templates. Schedule bi-weekly 30-minute home visits for first month, then monthly for 5 months. Develop referral pathways for readings above threshold values.
expected_outcomes: 11.7 mmHg greater reduction in systolic BP compared to usual care (95% CI: 8.2-15.2 mmHg), 5.4 mmHg greater reduction in diastolic BP (95% CI: 3.1-7.7 mmHg). NNT: 6 patients to achieve one additional controlled BP.
citation_authors: Margolis KL, Asche SE, Dehmer SP, Bergdall AR, Green BB, Sperl-Hillen JM, et al.
citation_title: Long-term outcomes of the effects of home blood pressure telemonitoring and pharmacist management on blood pressure among adults with uncontrolled hypertension: Follow-up of a cluster randomized clinical trial
target_population: Adults with uncontrolled hypertension
cost_effectiveness: $1,850 per quality-adjusted life year gained

title: Behavioral Health Depression Screening
recommendation_text: Implement systematic depression screening using PHQ-9 for all adult patients, with integrated behavioral health follow-up within 7 days for positive screens. Establish warm handoff protocols between primary care and behavioral health services.
implementation_guidance: Train all clinical staff on PHQ-9 administration and scoring. Create EHR templates for documentation and tracking. Develop workflow for same-day behavioral health consultations when possible. Establish registry for tracking patients with positive screens.
expected_outcomes: Increased depression identification by 27% (95% CI: 19-35%), 62% of patients with moderate-to-severe depression showing clinically significant improvement at 6 months. NNT: 5 patients screened to identify one case of previously undiagnosed depression.
citation_authors: US Preventive Services Task Force
citation_title: Screening for Depression and Suicide Risk in Adults: US Preventive Services Task Force Recommendation Statement
target_population: All adults, especially those with risk factors
cost_effectiveness: $3,200 per quality-adjusted life year gained

title: Peer Support Substance Use Recovery
recommendation_text: Provide weekly peer recovery support services for individuals with substance use disorders, focusing on recovery planning, resource navigation, and social support. Integrate peer support with clinical treatment services and community resources.
implementation_guidance: Schedule initial 90-minute assessment to develop personalized recovery plan. Conduct weekly 60-minute individual or group sessions. Train peers in motivational interviewing and CCAR Recovery Coach model. Implement standardized documentation system for recovery goals and progress.
expected_outcomes: 47% reduction in substance use (95% CI: 38-56%), 42% improvement in treatment retention, 35% reduction in emergency department visits. NNT: 4 patients to prevent one treatment dropout.
citation_authors: Eddie D, Hoffman L, Vilsaint C, Abry A, Bergman B, Hoeppner B, et al.
citation_title: Lived Experience in New Models of Care for Substance Use Disorder: A Systematic Review of Peer Recovery Support Services and Recovery Coaching
target_population: Individuals with substance use disorders
cost_effectiveness: Cost savings of $2,400 per patient annually in healthcare utilization

title: Care Coordinator Chronic Disease Management
recommendation_text: Implement nurse-led care coordination program with monthly patient contact to address care gaps, coordinate specialist appointments, and provide self-management support. Utilize risk stratification to identify high-need patients for more intensive intervention.
implementation_guidance: Develop risk stratification algorithm using clinical and social determinants data. Create care coordination documentation templates. Schedule monthly 30-minute check-ins via phone or video. Establish communication protocols with primary care and specialty providers.
expected_outcomes: 23% reduction in all-cause hospitalizations (95% CI: 17-29%), 32% reduction in emergency department visits, 18% improvement in medication adherence. NNT: 9 patients to prevent one hospitalization.
citation_authors: Joo JY, Liu MF
citation_title: Effectiveness of Nurse-Led Case Management in Cancer Care: Systematic Review
target_population: Adults with multiple chronic conditions
cost_effectiveness: Return on investment of $1.80 per $1 spent

title: Social Worker Housing Intervention
recommendation_text: Provide comprehensive housing case management services for patients experiencing housing instability, including assessment, housing navigation, application assistance, and landlord mediation. Coordinate with community housing resources and legal aid services.
implementation_guidance: Conduct standardized housing instability assessment at intake. Create directory of local housing resources and eligibility requirements. Schedule weekly 45-60 minute case management sessions until housing is secured. Develop follow-up protocol for 6 months post-housing placement.
expected_outcomes: 73% of clients secure stable housing within 6 months (95% CI: 65-81%), 48% reduction in emergency department visits, 52% reduction in inpatient hospitalizations. NNT: 2 clients to achieve one stable housing placement.
citation_authors: Aubry T, Bloch G, Brcic V, Saad A, Magwood O, Abdalla T, et al.
citation_title: Effectiveness of permanent supportive housing and income assistance interventions for homeless individuals in high-income countries: A systematic review
target_population: Individuals experiencing housing instability
cost_effectiveness: Net savings of $6,300 per person in healthcare and social service costs

title: PCP Prediabetes Intervention
recommendation_text: Implement intensive lifestyle intervention program for patients with prediabetes, including structured diet and physical activity guidance, with quarterly monitoring of glycemic status. Refer eligible patients to CDC-recognized Diabetes Prevention Programs.
implementation_guidance: Screen all eligible patients for prediabetes using ADA risk assessment. Provide initial 30-minute counseling session on lifestyle modifications. Schedule quarterly follow-up visits for monitoring. Develop referral pathway to local DPP programs.
expected_outcomes: 58% reduction in progression to type 2 diabetes (95% CI: 48-66%), mean weight loss of 5-7% of initial body weight, improvements in cardiovascular risk factors. NNT: 7 patients to prevent one case of diabetes over 3 years.
citation_authors: Haw JS, Galaviz KI, Straus AN, Kowalski AJ, Magee MJ, Weber MB, et al.
citation_title: Long-term Sustainability of Diabetes Prevention Approaches: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials
target_population: Adults with prediabetes (A1C 5.7-6.4%)
cost_effectiveness: $7,300 per quality-adjusted life year gained

title: Doula Postpartum Support
recommendation_text: Provide 3-5 postpartum home visits within the first 6 weeks after birth to support breastfeeding, maternal recovery, newborn care, and mental health screening. Implement structured assessment for postpartum depression at each visit.
implementation_guidance: Schedule first visit within 3-5 days of birth. Conduct Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale screening at 2 weeks and 6 weeks postpartum. Provide hands-on breastfeeding support and education. Develop referral pathways for lactation specialists and mental health providers.
expected_outcomes: 62% increase in breastfeeding continuation at 6 weeks (95% CI: 53-71%), 44% reduction in postpartum depression diagnosis, improved maternal confidence scores. NNT: 5 mothers to prevent one case of breastfeeding discontinuation.
citation_authors: Kozhimannil KB, Hardeman RR, Attanasio LB, Blauer-Peterson C, O'Brien M
citation_title: Doula care, birth outcomes, and costs among Medicaid beneficiaries
target_population: Postpartum individuals, particularly those with limited social support
cost_effectiveness: Return on investment of $2.20 per $1 spent

title: Use Specific Motivational Interviewing Questions for Medication Adherence
recommendation_text: Ask patients to rate their confidence in taking medications as prescribed on a scale of 1-10, then follow up with 'What would help move that number higher?' to identify specific barriers. Document responses in the EHR and create an action plan addressing the top barrier identified.
implementation_guidance: Implement this technique during medication reconciliation at each visit. Document both the confidence rating and the specific barriers identified. Schedule a follow-up call within 2 weeks to assess progress on the action plan.
expected_outcomes: Improved medication adherence rates by 15-20% within 3 months, reduced adverse events related to medication non-adherence, and increased patient engagement in self-management.
target_population: Patients with chronic conditions requiring multiple medications
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention that can be implemented during routine visits with minimal additional time (2-3 minutes).
citation_authors: Palacio A, Garay D, Langer B, et al.
citation_title: Motivational Interviewing Improves Medication Adherence: a Systematic Review and Meta-analysis

title: Structured Telephone Follow-up After Hospital Discharge
recommendation_text: Call patients within 48-72 hours of hospital discharge using a structured script that asks: 1) Do you understand your discharge instructions? 2) Have you filled all prescribed medications? 3) Do you have transportation to your follow-up appointment? 4) Have any new symptoms developed? Document responses and escalate concerns to the primary care provider.
implementation_guidance: Assign responsibility for calls to a specific team member. Use a standardized documentation template in the EHR. Develop a clear protocol for escalating concerns identified during calls.
expected_outcomes: 20% reduction in 30-day readmissions, 30% increase in attendance at follow-up appointments, and improved patient satisfaction scores.
target_population: All patients discharged from inpatient care, with priority for high-risk patients (multiple chronic conditions, polypharmacy, prior readmissions)
cost_effectiveness: Moderate cost intervention that reduces expensive readmissions with an estimated ROI of $3 for every $1 invested.
citation_authors: Hansen LO, Young RS, Hinami K, et al.
citation_title: Interventions to reduce 30-day rehospitalization: a systematic review

title: Teach-Back Method for Medication Instructions
recommendation_text: After explaining a new medication, say: 'To make sure I explained this clearly, could you tell me how you'll take this medication at home?' Address any misunderstandings immediately and document the teach-back process in the patient record.
implementation_guidance: Use teach-back for all new medication prescriptions. If the patient cannot correctly explain, use different words (not just repeating) and check understanding again. Document both the use of teach-back and any areas requiring clarification.
expected_outcomes: 25% reduction in adverse drug events, improved medication adherence rates, and reduced emergency department visits related to medication errors.
target_population: All patients receiving new medication prescriptions, particularly those with low health literacy, cognitive impairment, or complex medication regimens
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention requiring minimal additional time (1-2 minutes per medication) with significant downstream cost savings.
citation_authors: Schillinger D, Piette J, Grumbach K, et al.
citation_title: Closing the loop: physician communication with diabetic patients who have low health literacy

title: Specific Screening Questions for Social Isolation
recommendation_text: Ask patients these three questions during intake: 1) 'How often do you feel that you lack companionship?' 2) 'How often do you feel left out?' 3) 'How often do you feel isolated from others?' For patients who answer 'often' to any question, provide a referral to community resources and schedule a follow-up assessment within 30 days.
implementation_guidance: Incorporate these questions into standard intake forms. Create a resource list of local community programs addressing social isolation. Document responses and referrals in the EHR.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 15-20% more socially isolated patients, 30% increase in referrals to community support programs, and improved depression screening scores at follow-up.
target_population: All adult patients, with particular attention to older adults, those living alone, and those with chronic conditions
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost screening with potential for significant impact on mental health outcomes and healthcare utilization.
citation_authors: Lubben J, Blozik E, Gillmann G, et al.
citation_title: Performance of an abbreviated version of the Lubben Social Network Scale among three European community-dwelling older adult populations

title: Structured Physical Activity Prescription
recommendation_text: Write a specific physical activity prescription that includes: 1) Type of activity (e.g., walking, swimming) 2) Frequency (days per week) 3) Duration (minutes per session) 4) Intensity (e.g., moderate - able to talk but not sing). Provide the prescription in writing and document in the EHR.
implementation_guidance: Use a pre-printed prescription pad or EHR template. Start with achievable goals based on current activity level. Schedule follow-up to assess adherence and adjust prescription as needed.
expected_outcomes: 30% increase in patient-reported physical activity levels, improved cardiovascular metrics, and weight management outcomes.
target_population: Sedentary adults and those with conditions that would benefit from increased physical activity (cardiovascular disease, diabetes, obesity, depression)
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with potential for significant impact on chronic disease management and prevention.
citation_authors: Orrow G, Kinmonth AL, Sanderson S, et al.
citation_title: Effectiveness of physical activity promotion based in primary care: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials

title: Specific Food Insecurity Screening Questions
recommendation_text: Ask these two validated questions during intake: 1) 'Within the past 12 months, we worried whether our food would run out before we got money to buy more.' 2) 'Within the past 12 months, the food we bought just didn't last and we didn't have money to get more.' Document responses as 'often true,' 'sometimes true,' or 'never true' and provide immediate referral to food assistance programs for any 'often true' or 'sometimes true' responses.
implementation_guidance: Incorporate questions into standard intake forms. Maintain an updated list of local food resources including food banks, SNAP enrollment assistance, and meal delivery programs. Create a flagging system in the EHR for positive screens.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 10-15% more food insecure patients, 40% increase in referrals to food assistance programs, and improved management of nutrition-sensitive conditions.
target_population: All patients, with particular attention to those with limited income, chronic disease, or families with children
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost screening with high potential impact on health outcomes and healthcare utilization.
citation_authors: Hager ER, Quigg AM, Black MM, et al.
citation_title: Development and validity of a 2-item screen to identify families at risk for food insecurity

title: Specific Questions to Assess Medication Cost Barriers
recommendation_text: Ask patients: 1) 'In the past 30 days, have you skipped or taken less medication to make it last longer?' 2) 'Do you ever have difficulty paying for your medications?' For patients who answer 'yes' to either question, immediately review medication list for lower-cost alternatives, provide information on prescription assistance programs, and document the intervention in the EHR.
implementation_guidance: Incorporate questions into medication reconciliation process. Maintain an updated list of prescription assistance programs and lower-cost pharmacy options. Train staff on available resources for medication assistance.
expected_outcomes: 20% reduction in cost-related medication non-adherence, improved chronic disease control metrics, and reduced emergency department visits.
target_population: All patients on prescription medications, particularly those with multiple chronic conditions, fixed incomes, or high-cost specialty medications
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential to improve medication adherence and reduce downstream healthcare costs.
citation_authors: Patel MR, Piette JD, Resnicow K, et al.
citation_title: Improving Medication Adherence by Addressing Medication Cost Concerns

title: Structured Approach to Assess Transportation Barriers
recommendation_text: Ask patients: 1) 'Do you have reliable transportation to medical appointments?' 2) 'In the past 6 months, have you missed or rescheduled appointments due to transportation problems?' 3) 'What type of transportation do you typically use to get to appointments?' For patients identifying transportation barriers, provide information on available transportation services and document in the EHR.
implementation_guidance: Incorporate questions into pre-visit planning or intake process. Maintain an updated list of transportation resources including Medicaid transportation benefits, community shuttle services, and rideshare programs. Create a flagging system for patients with transportation barriers.
expected_outcomes: 25% reduction in missed appointments, improved chronic disease management metrics, and increased patient satisfaction.
target_population: All patients, with particular attention to older adults, those with disabilities, low-income patients, and rural residents
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost screening with potential for significant impact on appointment adherence and healthcare utilization.
citation_authors: Syed ST, Gerber BS, Sharp LK
citation_title: Traveling towards disease: transportation barriers to health care access

title: Specific Health Literacy Assessment Technique
recommendation_text: Ask patients to read the instructions on a medication bottle and explain in their own words what they mean. Note any difficulties or misunderstandings, and use this information to tailor education approaches. For patients with identified literacy challenges, use visual aids and teach-back methods for all instructions.
implementation_guidance: Implement during medication reconciliation or when providing new prescriptions. Document health literacy assessment and preferred education methods in the EHR. Use a standardized approach across team members.
expected_outcomes: Improved patient understanding of medication instructions, 30% reduction in medication errors, and increased patient confidence in self-management.
target_population: All patients, with particular attention to those with limited education, non-native English speakers, and older adults
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost assessment with significant potential to improve medication safety and adherence.
citation_authors: Davis TC, Wolf MS, Bass PF, et al.
citation_title: Literacy and misunderstanding prescription drug labels

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Caregiver Burden
recommendation_text: Ask caregivers: 1) 'Do you feel overwhelmed by your caregiving responsibilities?' 2) 'Do you have time to take care of your own health needs?' 3) 'Would you like information about resources to help with caregiving?' For caregivers expressing burden, provide immediate referral to respite services and caregiver support programs.
implementation_guidance: Incorporate questions into visits when caregivers are present. Maintain an updated list of caregiver support resources including respite care, support groups, and educational programs. Document caregiver assessment and referrals in the patient's EHR.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 25% more caregivers experiencing burden, 35% increase in referrals to support services, and improved health outcomes for both caregivers and care recipients.
target_population: Family caregivers of patients with chronic conditions, disabilities, or cognitive impairment
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost assessment with potential for significant impact on caregiver health and patient care quality.
citation_authors: Adelman RD, Tmanova LL, Delgado D, et al.
citation_title: Caregiver burden: a clinical review

title: Structured Approach for Assessing Fall Risk
recommendation_text: Conduct a standardized fall risk assessment using the Timed Up and Go (TUG) test by asking the patient to rise from a chair, walk 10 feet, turn around, walk back, and sit down. Document the time taken and observe for unsteadiness. For patients taking >12 seconds or showing unsteadiness, implement a personalized fall prevention plan.
implementation_guidance: Perform assessment during routine visits for all patients 65+ or those with balance concerns. Use a standard chair (seat height 18 inches) and mark the 10-foot distance clearly. Document results in a dedicated fall risk section of the EHR.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 25% more patients at risk for falls, 30% reduction in fall incidents among identified high-risk patients, and decreased fall-related emergency department visits.
target_population: Adults 65+ and younger patients with neurological conditions, balance disorders, or multiple medications
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost screening (under $5 per patient) with potential for significant cost savings from prevented falls ($14,000+ per fall-related hospitalization).
citation_authors: Lusardi MM, Fritz S, Middleton A, et al.
citation_title: Determining Risk of Falls in Community Dwelling Older Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis Using Posttest Probability

title: Specific Technique for Medication Reconciliation
recommendation_text: Ask patients to bring all medications (prescription, over-the-counter, supplements) to each visit in their original containers. Compare with the medication list in the EHR by asking: 1) 'How do you actually take this medication?' 2) 'Do you ever skip doses or take it differently than prescribed?' 3) 'Have you stopped taking any medications?' Document all discrepancies and update the medication list.
implementation_guidance: Send medication bag reminder before appointments. Allocate 5-10 minutes for reconciliation. Use a standardized documentation template. Flag high-risk medications (anticoagulants, insulin, opioids) for special attention.
expected_outcomes: Identification of medication discrepancies in 40-60% of patients, 25% reduction in adverse drug events, and improved accuracy of medication lists.
target_population: All patients on multiple medications, particularly during care transitions, older adults, and those with complex medication regimens
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential to reduce medication errors and related hospitalizations.
citation_authors: Mueller SK, Sponsler KC, Kripalani S, et al.
citation_title: Hospital-based medication reconciliation practices: a systematic review

title: Specific Questions for Assessing Medication Understanding
recommendation_text: For each new medication, ask patients these four questions: 1) 'What is the name of this medication?' 2) 'What is it for?' 3) 'How much do you take and when?' 4) 'What side effects should you watch for?' Document areas of misunderstanding and provide targeted education to address knowledge gaps.
implementation_guidance: Implement during medication counseling for all new prescriptions. Use plain language explanations for medical terms. Provide written information at appropriate literacy level. Document patient's understanding in the EHR.
expected_outcomes: Improved patient knowledge of medications by 40%, 30% reduction in medication errors, and increased patient confidence in medication self-management.
target_population: All patients receiving new medications, particularly those with limited health literacy, cognitive impairment, or complex medication regimens
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention requiring minimal additional time with potential for significant reduction in medication-related adverse events.
citation_authors: Marvanova M, Roumie CL, Eden SK, et al.
citation_title: Health literacy and medication understanding among hospitalized adults

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Inhaler Technique
recommendation_text: Ask patients to demonstrate how they use their inhaler with a placebo device. Observe for specific errors in technique: 1) Failure to exhale before inhalation 2) Improper seal around mouthpiece 3) Inadequate breath hold after inhalation 4) Incorrect timing of actuation. Provide immediate correction and re-demonstration until proper technique is achieved.
implementation_guidance: Assess technique at initial prescription and at least annually thereafter. Keep placebo inhalers for all commonly prescribed devices. Document specific errors observed and corrections provided in the EHR.
expected_outcomes: Identification of technique errors in 60-80% of patients, 25% improvement in symptom control after technique correction, and reduced emergency department visits for respiratory exacerbations.
target_population: All patients using inhaled medications, particularly those with asthma or COPD
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential to improve medication effectiveness and reduce acute care utilization.
citation_authors: Sanchis J, Gich I, Pedersen S, et al.
citation_title: Systematic Review of Errors in Inhaler Use: Has Patient Technique Improved Over Time?

title: Specific Approach for Addressing Vaccine Hesitancy
recommendation_text: Use the CASE approach when discussing vaccines: C (Corroborate) - acknowledge the patient's concerns; A (About me) - share your expertise and experience; S (Science) - explain the scientific evidence; E (Explain/Advise) - provide a clear recommendation. Document the specific concerns raised and your response.
implementation_guidance: Implement during preventive care visits or when vaccines are due. Avoid dismissing concerns or overwhelming with statistics. Use motivational interviewing techniques to explore barriers. Document the conversation and follow-up plan.
expected_outcomes: 15-20% increase in vaccine acceptance among hesitant patients, improved patient-provider trust, and increased overall vaccination rates.
target_population: Patients expressing vaccine hesitancy or refusing recommended vaccines
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant public health benefits and potential reduction in vaccine-preventable diseases.
citation_authors: Jacobson RM, St. Sauver JL, Finney Rutten LJ
citation_title: Vaccine Hesitancy

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Suicidal Ideation
recommendation_text: Ask these three direct questions in sequence: 1) 'Have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead or of hurting yourself in some way?' If yes, ask: 2) 'Have you had thoughts of how you might do this?' If yes, ask: 3) 'Have you had intentions to act on these thoughts?' Document responses verbatim and implement appropriate safety planning based on risk level.
implementation_guidance: Ask questions in a private setting. Maintain a calm, matter-of-fact tone. Have crisis resources immediately available. Document risk assessment, safety plan, and follow-up arrangements in the EHR.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 30% more patients with suicidal ideation, appropriate risk stratification, and reduced suicide attempts through timely intervention.
target_population: All patients with depression, substance use disorders, recent life crises, or previous suicide attempts
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost screening with potential for life-saving interventions and prevention of costly emergency services.
citation_authors: Posner K, Brown GK, Stanley B, et al.
citation_title: The Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Scale: initial validity and internal consistency findings from three multisite studies with adolescents and adults

title: Specific Approach for Medication Adherence Barriers
recommendation_text: Ask patients who are not taking medications as prescribed: 1) 'What makes it difficult to take your medication?' 2) 'What would make it easier?' 3) 'What have you tried that has helped?' Based on responses, implement targeted interventions such as dose simplification, reminder systems, or cost assistance.
implementation_guidance: Use a non-judgmental approach. Focus on practical solutions rather than emphasizing non-adherence. Document specific barriers identified and interventions implemented. Schedule follow-up to assess effectiveness.
expected_outcomes: Identification of specific adherence barriers in 80% of non-adherent patients, 25-30% improvement in medication adherence rates, and better disease control metrics.
target_population: Patients with chronic conditions requiring long-term medication therapy, particularly those with demonstrated non-adherence
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential to improve treatment effectiveness and reduce complications.
citation_authors: Zullig LL, Bosworth HB
citation_title: Engaging Patients to Optimize Medication Adherence

title: Specific Technique for Pain Assessment in Non-verbal Patients
recommendation_text: Use the PAINAD (Pain Assessment in Advanced Dementia) scale to assess pain in non-verbal patients by observing: 1) Breathing 2) Negative vocalization 3) Facial expression 4) Body language 5) Consolability. Score each category from 0-2 and document total score (0-10). Implement pain management interventions for scores ≥4.
implementation_guidance: Assess during rest and with movement. Observe for at least 5 minutes. Compare scores over time to evaluate treatment effectiveness. Document scores and interventions in the EHR.
expected_outcomes: Improved pain detection in 40% of non-verbal patients, more appropriate analgesic administration, and reduced distress behaviors.
target_population: Non-verbal patients, particularly those with dementia, cognitive impairment, or communication disorders
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost assessment with potential for significant improvement in quality of life and reduction in distress behaviors.
citation_authors: Warden V, Hurley AC, Volicer L
citation_title: Development and psychometric evaluation of the Pain Assessment in Advanced Dementia (PAINAD) scale
citation_journal: Journal of the American Medical Directors Association

title: Specific Approach for Addressing Health Literacy in Discharge Instructions
recommendation_text: Use the teach-back method for discharge instructions by saying: 'I want to make sure I explained your care plan clearly. Can you tell me in your own words: 1) What health problem you were treated for 2) What medications you need to take 3) What warning signs to watch for 4) When your follow-up appointment is?' Address any misunderstandings before discharge.
implementation_guidance: Implement for all discharges. Use plain language without medical jargon. Provide written instructions at 5th-6th grade reading level. Document use of teach-back and areas requiring clarification.
expected_outcomes: 30% reduction in post-discharge medication errors, 25% reduction in readmissions, and improved patient satisfaction with discharge process.
target_population: All patients being discharged from inpatient care, particularly those with limited health literacy, complex discharge plans, or high risk for readmission
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with significant potential to reduce costly readmissions and post-discharge complications.
citation_authors: Teach-back Collaborative
citation_title: Always Use Teach-back! Training Toolkit

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Alcohol Use
recommendation_text: Use the AUDIT-C three-question screening: 1) 'How often do you have a drink containing alcohol?' 2) 'How many drinks do you have on a typical day when you are drinking?' 3) 'How often do you have six or more drinks on one occasion?' Score each question 0-4 and implement brief intervention for scores ≥4 (men) or ≥3 (women).
implementation_guidance: Screen annually for all adult patients. Use a matter-of-fact, non-judgmental approach. For positive screens, conduct brief intervention using motivational interviewing techniques. Document scores and interventions in the EHR.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 20-30% more patients with unhealthy alcohol use, 15-20% reduction in alcohol consumption among those receiving brief intervention, and increased referrals to treatment.
target_population: All adult patients, with particular attention to those with conditions that may be exacerbated by alcohol use
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost screening with potential for significant reduction in alcohol-related health problems and healthcare utilization.
citation_authors: Bush K, Kivlahan DR, McDonell MB, et al.
citation_title: The AUDIT alcohol consumption questions (AUDIT-C): an effective brief screening test for problem drinking

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Dyspnea
recommendation_text: Use the modified Borg scale (0-10) to assess dyspnea by asking: 'On a scale of 0 to 10, where 0 is no breathlessness and 10 is the worst breathlessness imaginable, how would you rate your breathing right now?' Document the score and compare to previous ratings to evaluate treatment effectiveness.
implementation_guidance: Assess at rest and with activity. Use a visual scale with descriptors. Document scores in a consistent location in the EHR. Implement oxygen assessment for scores ≥5.
expected_outcomes: More accurate assessment of dyspnea severity, improved titration of respiratory treatments, and better documentation of symptom progression or improvement.
target_population: Patients with respiratory conditions, particularly COPD, asthma, heart failure, or interstitial lung disease
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost assessment with potential for improved symptom management and reduced emergency visits.
citation_authors: Kendrick KR, Baxi SC, Smith RM
citation_title: Usefulness of the modified 0-10 Borg scale in assessing the degree of dyspnea in patients with COPD and asthma

title: Specific Questions for Assessing Medication Side Effects
recommendation_text: Ask patients these specific questions about medication side effects: 1) 'Since starting this medication, have you noticed any new symptoms or problems?' 2) 'Have you changed how you take this medication because of any side effects?' 3) 'Are there any side effects that concern you enough to consider stopping the medication?' Document responses and address concerns immediately.
implementation_guidance: Ask during medication reviews and follow-up visits. Use open-ended questions first, followed by specific questions about common side effects of each medication. Document side effects reported and actions taken.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 25-30% more medication side effects, improved patient satisfaction with medication management, and reduced self-discontinuation of medications.
target_population: All patients on prescription medications, particularly those newly started on medications with significant side effect profiles
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with potential for improved medication adherence and early identification of adverse effects.
citation_authors: Basch E, Deal AM, Kris MG, et al.
citation_title: Symptom Monitoring With Patient-Reported Outcomes During Routine Cancer Treatment: A Randomized Controlled Trial

title: Specific Approach for Addressing Low Health Literacy
recommendation_text: Use the 'chunk and check' method when providing complex information: 1) Break information into small, manageable chunks 2) Present one chunk at a time 3) Check understanding before moving to the next chunk by asking 'What questions do you have about what I just explained?' Document areas requiring additional explanation.
implementation_guidance: Implement for all patient education, particularly for complex treatment plans or procedures. Use plain language (6th grade level or below). Supplement verbal information with visual aids when possible.
expected_outcomes: Improved patient comprehension of health information, increased adherence to treatment plans, and reduced errors in self-management.
target_population: All patients, particularly those with limited health literacy, limited English proficiency, or cognitive impairment
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with potential for significant improvement in treatment adherence and outcomes.
citation_authors: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality
citation_title: Health Literacy Universal Precautions Toolkit

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Frailty
recommendation_text: Perform the FRAIL scale assessment by asking about: F (Fatigue) - 'Are you fatigued?' R (Resistance) - 'Can you climb one flight of stairs?' A (Ambulation) - 'Can you walk one block?' I (Illnesses) - 'Do you have more than 5 illnesses?' L (Loss of weight) - 'Have you lost more than 5% of weight in the past 6 months?' Score 1 point for each 'yes' to F, I, L or 'no' to R, A. Implement comprehensive geriatric assessment for scores ≥3.
implementation_guidance: Screen annually for all patients 65+ or those with multiple chronic conditions. Document scores in a dedicated section of the EHR. Develop referral pathways for physical therapy, nutrition, and geriatric consultation based on results.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 15-20% more frail patients, earlier intervention to prevent functional decline, and reduced hospitalizations and falls.
target_population: Adults 65+ and younger patients with multiple chronic conditions or functional limitations
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost screening with potential for significant reduction in healthcare utilization and institutional care costs.
citation_authors: Morley JE, Malmstrom TK, Miller DK
citation_title: A simple frailty questionnaire (FRAIL) predicts outcomes in middle aged African Americans

title: Specific Approach for Addressing Medication Cost Concerns
recommendation_text: When patients express medication cost concerns, take these specific actions: 1) Review current medications for potential generic substitutions 2) Check for therapeutic alternatives in lower cost tiers 3) Investigate patient assistance programs 4) Consider 90-day supplies to reduce copays 5) Document interventions in the EHR and follow up within 2 weeks to ensure medication access.
implementation_guidance: Train staff to identify cost concern cues. Create a resource list of patient assistance programs. Develop protocols for pharmacist consultation when cost barriers are identified. Document cost-related interventions in a consistent location.
expected_outcomes: 25-30% reduction in cost-related medication non-adherence, improved affordability of prescribed regimens, and better chronic disease control.
target_population: Patients expressing medication cost concerns, those with high out-of-pocket costs, and those with multiple medications
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with potential for significant improvement in medication adherence and disease outcomes.
citation_authors: Viswanathan M, Golin CE, Jones CD, et al.
citation_title: Interventions to Improve Adherence to Self-administered Medications for Chronic Diseases in the United States: A Systematic Review

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Caregiver Strain
recommendation_text: Use the Modified Caregiver Strain Index by asking caregivers 13 specific yes/no questions about: sleep disruption, inconvenience, physical strain, confinement, family adjustments, changes in personal plans, emotional adjustments, upsetting behaviors, time demands, and feelings of being overwhelmed. Score 1 point for each 'yes' and provide immediate support resources for scores ≥7.
implementation_guidance: Assess at least annually for all primary caregivers. Create a private setting for assessment. Develop a resource list of caregiver support services. Document scores and referrals provided.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 30-40% more caregivers experiencing significant strain, increased referrals to support services, and reduced caregiver burnout.
target_population: Family caregivers of patients with chronic conditions, disabilities, or cognitive impairment
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost assessment with potential for significant impact on caregiver health and patient care quality.
citation_authors: Thornton M, Travis SS
citation_title: Analysis of the reliability of the Modified Caregiver Strain Index
citation_journal: The Journals of Gerontology, Series B

title: Specific Approach for Addressing Medication Adherence in Depression
recommendation_text: For patients prescribed antidepressants, implement these specific strategies: 1) Explain that full benefits may take 2-4 weeks 2) Discuss specific side effects to expect and how long they typically last 3) Schedule follow-up at 2 weeks to assess side effects 4) Use reminder systems tailored to patient preference 5) Document adherence barriers and interventions.
implementation_guidance: Implement at initial prescription and reinforce at follow-up visits. Provide both verbal and written information. Create a follow-up system to check in with patients within the first week of starting medication. Document specific barriers identified and strategies implemented.
expected_outcomes: 30-40% improvement in antidepressant adherence at 3 months, reduced premature discontinuation, and improved depression outcomes.
target_population: Patients newly prescribed antidepressant medications or those with history of non-adherence
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost intervention with potential for significant improvement in depression outcomes and reduced healthcare utilization.
citation_authors: Fortney JC, Pyne JM, Edlund MJ, et al.
citation_title: A randomized trial of telemedicine-based collaborative care for depression

title: Specific Technique for Assessing Nutrition Risk
recommendation_text: Use the DETERMINE checklist to assess nutrition risk by asking about: Disease, Eating poorly, Tooth loss/mouth pain, Economic hardship, Reduced social contact, Multiple medications, Involuntary weight loss/gain, Needs assistance in self-care, and Elder years above 80. Score 1 point for each risk factor present and implement nutrition intervention for scores ≥3.
implementation_guidance: Screen annually for all older adults and those with chronic conditions. Create a standardized documentation template. Develop referral pathways to dietitians, food assistance programs, and meal delivery services based on identified risks.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 20-25% more patients with nutrition risk, increased appropriate referrals to nutrition services, and improved nutritional status.
target_population: Older adults, those with chronic conditions affecting nutrition, and those with recent weight changes
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost screening with potential for significant impact on health outcomes and functional status.
citation_authors: Posner BM, Jette AM, Smith KW, Miller DR
citation_title: Nutrition and health risks in the elderly: the nutrition screening initiative

title: Specific Questions for Assessing Sleep Quality
recommendation_text: Ask patients these specific questions about sleep: 1) 'How long does it typically take you to fall asleep?' 2) 'How many times do you wake up during the night?' 3) 'How many hours of sleep do you get each night?' 4) 'Do you feel rested when you wake up?' 5) 'Does poor sleep affect your daily activities?' Document responses and implement sleep hygiene education for identified problems.
implementation_guidance: Incorporate questions into routine health assessments. Create a sleep hygiene handout with specific recommendations. Document sleep patterns and interventions in the EHR. Consider referral to sleep specialist for patients with significant disruption.
expected_outcomes: Identification of 30-40% more patients with sleep disorders, improved sleep quality through non-pharmacological interventions, and reduced inappropriate use of sleep medications.
target_population: All adult patients, particularly those with chronic conditions, mental health disorders, or complaints of fatigue
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost assessment with potential for improved quality of life and reduced healthcare utilization.
citation_authors: Buysse DJ
citation_title: Sleep Health: Can We Define It? Does It Matter?

title: Specific Approach for Addressing Chronic Pain
recommendation_text: Implement the 4 A's approach for chronic pain management: 1) Analgesia - Ask 'On a scale of 0-10, how would you rate your pain before and after taking medication?' 2) Activities - Ask 'What activities can you do when your pain is controlled?' 3) Adverse effects - Ask 'What side effects are you experiencing from pain medications?' 4) Aberrant behaviors - Monitor for concerning patterns. Document all four components at each visit.
implementation_guidance: Use at every visit for patients with chronic pain. Create a standardized documentation template. Develop clear protocols for addressing concerning findings. Schedule regular reassessment of pain management effectiveness.
expected_outcomes: More comprehensive assessment of pain treatment effectiveness, improved functional outcomes, and earlier identification of medication-related problems.
target_population: Patients with chronic pain conditions, particularly those on long-term pain medications
cost_effectiveness: Low-cost assessment with potential for improved pain management and reduced complications from pain treatments.
citation_authors: Passik SD, Weinreb HJ
citation_title: Managing chronic nonmalignant pain: overcoming obstacles to the use of opioids
